primitives.name: Behavioral Adaptation Introspection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first point, we would make, is that in introspection the "environmental" objects, about which the introspector is talking, and which his proclamations purport to bring to the listener's attention, are the introspector's own behavior-adjustments.
primitives.assumptions: The introspector can produce verbal utterances as tools to communicate their own behavioral adjustments to others.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when the introspective act cannot be decoupled from the underlying behavioral adjustment, leading to circularity.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction intervals where the introspective report serves as a calibration set for internal model validity.
layer2.telemetry: Measurable discrepancies between reported behavioral adjustments and actual observable actions.

primitives.name: Inner Sense Perception
primitives.verbatim_quote: -hort Introspection, if it be a veridical process at all, implies, in short, some sort of an "inner sense." It implies that the introspector can "perceive" not only his actual runnings-back-and-forth, but also his mere behavior-adjustments to such runnings-back-and-forth.
primitives.assumptions: The introspector possesses a perceptual mechanism that operates on their own behavioral patterns rather than external stimuli.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the introspective feedback loop becomes unstable, causing misinterpretation of self-generated signals.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to GSE state-transition logic where an agent monitors its own internal state transitions to predict future moves.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking the consistency of self-reported behavioral states against recorded action sequences.

primitives.name: Verbal Tool Behavior
primitives.verbatim_quote: Introspection requires, if any credence is to be given to it, that an individual can release tool-behavior in which the utterance of the words is the means-commerce and the presence-to-the-listener of the introspector's own behavior-adjustments is the goal-object.
primitives.assumptions: Language functions as a behavioral tool designed to achieve specific social objectives related to self-disclosure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses when the verbal communication fails to accurately represent the intended behavioral adjustment, resulting in miscommunication.

layer2.mapping: Corresponds to GSI information transfer models where linguistic expressions serve as compressed representations of complex behavioral data.
layer2.telemetry: Quantifying the efficiency of information compression in verbal reports compared to direct behavioral observation.

reasoning_traces.think:
The three primitives formalize introspection as a specialized form of tool-based communication. They describe how individuals use language to externally represent their own internal behavioral adjustments, requiring both an 'inner sense' for perception and a capacity for producing verbal tools that can convey these private states. Mathematically, this framework reveals introspection as a recursive system: the introspector must be able to observe their own behavior, categorize it into abstract 'adjustments,' and then encode those categories into linguistic symbols. This process inherently introduces potential failure modes—such as circularity when the introspective act itself alters the behavior being observed—or breakdowns when the mapping between private behavioral patterns and public linguistic expressions becomes corrupted. The primitives also highlight the duality between the internal state (the behavioral adjustment) and the external representation (the verbal report), establishing a clear boundary condition for when introspection can be considered valid versus when it becomes merely self-referential noise.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The conceptual roots trace back to classical empiricist theories of mind, particularly the British Associationists and early cognitive psychologists who viewed mental processes as analogous to physical behaviors. This lineage connects to modern computational theories of mind, especially those emphasizing embodied cognition and the role of language in structuring internal experience. The formalization builds upon cybernetic principles of feedback loops and control systems, originally developed during the mid-twentieth century.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: For an opposing agent, understanding these primitives suggests that introspective reports should not be treated as direct windows into the introspector's mind. Instead, they are filtered through the constraints of verbal tool production and the introspector's ability to perceive their own adjustments. A theory-of-mind approach would require modeling the introspector's competence in generating accurate reports, accounting for potential biases or limitations in their inner sense.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity conditions arise when multiple introspective primitives overlap in their functional requirements, creating redundant representations that degrade predictive power. For instance, if both 'inner sense' and 'verbal tool behavior' rely on the same neural substrate, their simultaneous activation could lead to interference. Leakage vetoes apply when external environmental factors (e.g., social pressure) inadvertently influence the introspective process, contaminating the pure behavioral adaptation signal with extraneous variables.
